To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

attention and multisensoral processing are linked in multiple ways, and that these links are bidirectional, with attentional processes influencing multisensory integration and with multisensory integration influencing attention.
attention can be captured by crossmodal interactions and can spread across sensory modalities to facilitate multisensory integration.
attention is required to facilitate the integration of crossmodal information, but that attention can also be automatically captured by multisensory events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between attentional mechanisms and multisensory perception.
the role of attention in modulating multisensory integration, and the role of multisensory integration in capturing and modulating attention.
the role of attention in the integration of information across the different sensory modalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attention is not a necessary condition for multisensory integration, but it can facilitate and enhance it.
attention can be modulated, and in turn modulates the integration of multisensorial stimuli.
multisensory processing can occur in the absence of attentional mechanisms, but that attentional mechanisms can also facilitate and modulate multisensory integration in various ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multisensory interactions can occur at multiple levels of processing, from early sensory to higher cognitive stages.
multisensory processing is a flexible, dynamic process that is shaped by attention and can shape attention.
multisensory processing is a dynamic, flexible process that can be modulated in a top down fashion by attention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interplay between attention, multisensory integration, and multisensory attention can best be described by a flexible, dynamic, and bidirectional relationship.
attention and multisensoral interactions are not separate, but rather, they are intimately linked and mutually modulatory processes.
the relationship between attention and multisensor integration is complex, dynamic and highly dependent on the nature of the multisensory event and the task at hand.
